title: A protocol for Asymmetric-Flow Field-Flow Fractionation \(AF4) of small extracellular vesicles
protocol: Deplete exosomes from FBS by ultracentrifugation at 100,000 x g at 10°C for 90 min.
Filter the FBS supernatant after ultracentrifugation using a 0.2μm filter unit to obtain exo-depleted FBS.
Prepare complete medium by supplementing DMEM with exo-depleted FBS, L-Glutamine, and Penicillin-Streptomycin Solution.
Seed ~2.25x10^6 B16-F10 cells per P150 tissue culture plate in 25ml of the complete medium.
Culture seeded plates in a humidified incubator for 72 h at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Collect conditioned media from plates into Falcon tubes.
Centrifuge collected media at 500 x g at 10°C for 10 min to remove cellular debris.
Transfer supernatant to ultracentrifuge tubes and centrifuge at 12,000 x g at 10°C for 20 min to remove apoptotic bodies and large microvesicles.
Transfer the supernatant to new ultracentrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge at 100,000 x g at 10°C for 70 minutes.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellets in 1 mL of ice-cold PBS per tube.
Combine all samples into one ultracentrifuge tube and raise the final volume to 50 mL with PBS.
Centrifuge at 100,000 x g at 10°C for another 70 minutes.
Resuspend the final pellet in approximately 0.5 mL of PBS on ice.
Transfer the resuspended sample to 1.7 mL microcentrifuge tubes on ice.
Quantify the yield by measuring protein concentration using the BCA kit.
Keep samples on ice overnight or freeze at -80°C for long-term storage.
Adjust the sEVs concentration to 1 µg/µL with PBS and spin at 12,000 x g at 4°C for 5 minutes before loading onto AF4.
Remove large protein and nanoparticle aggregates by centrifuging.
Transfer the supernatant into a pre-chilled screw cap vial.
Load 100 µg of input sample per run using the autosampler.
Start the AF4 fractionation with chosen parameters.
Separate samples in a short channel with a 10 kDa molecular weight cutoff membrane and 490 m spacer.
Operate the fractionation using the Eclipse AF4 system connected to an Agilent Technologies 1260 series iso pump, degasser, autosampler, and fraction collector.
Maintain autopsamplers and fraction collectors at 4 °C during the fractionation process.
Use PBS filtered with a 100 nm inline filter as the running buffer.
Monitor the system online using a UV detector (MWL) at 280 nm and a DAWN HELEOS II MALS detector at 664 nm, equipped with an internal QELS DLS detector installed at position 100°.
Set forward channel flow to 1 ml/min for detection.
Perform elution with Vx cross flow at 0.5 ml/min for 2 minutes.
Focus using Vx at 0.5 ml/min for 1 minute.
Inject samples while focusing and injecting simultaneously at Vx 0.5 ml/min and inject flow 0.2 ml/min for 2 minutes.
Separate samples with a gradient elution of Vx from 0.5 to 0 ml/min over 45 minutes, decreasing linearly.
Elute continuously at Vx 0 ml/min for 5 minutes.
Continue the process with an elute and inject step at Vx 0 ml/min for 5 minutes.
Collect fractionated samples into a 96-well plate based on time slices of 0.5 minutes per fraction using Agilent Fraction Collector.
Operate AF4 flow using Chemstation software with integrated Eclipse module.
Use Astra 6 for MALS, DLS and UV data acquisition and analysis.
Set data collection interval to 1 sec and QELS interval to 2 sec.
Deduce hydrodynamic radius of particles from DLS using literature equations.
Examine autocorrelation function at representative time points to determine fractionation efficiency.
Further examine individual representative fractions for morphology by TEM.
Transfer adjacent fractions with similar parameters to 50 mL Falcon tubes after examination.
Combine pooled fractions and concentrate them using Millipore centrifugal filter columns with Ultracel-30 membrane (30 kDa cutoff).
Pre-rinse filter columns by adding 5 mL or 15 mL ice-cold PBS, depending on the column type.
Spin pre-rinsed columns at 3,700 x g at 4°C for 5 minutes.
Discard flow-through and liquid remaining in top filter columns.
Transfer pooled fractionated samples into the top filter column.
Spin at 3,700 x g at 4°C for 7-8 minutes.
Retain concentrated samples in the top filter columns; discard the flow-through collected in bottom collection tubes.
Repeat step to concentrate each sample until desired volume is achieved.
Transfer concentrated samples to 1.7 mL microcentrifuge tubes on ice.
Record the volume of each concentrated sample.
Take aliquots for BCA assay to determine protein concentration.
Keep concentrated samples on ice for short-term storage or freeze at -80°C for long-term storage.
